chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah support him, informed me of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two عليهما السلام, who said:
The night of the seventeenth of the month of Ramadan, and it is the night of

and the night of the nineteenth, in which the delegation of the year is written; and the night of the twenty-first, which is the night in which the awsiya' of the Prophets were struck, and in it 'Isa ibn Maryam عليه السلام was raised and Musa عليه السلام was taken; and the night of the twenty-third, in which Laylat al-Qadr is hoped for; and the two days of the two 'Ids; and when you enter the two sanctuaries; and the day you enter ihram; and the day of visitation; and the day you enter the House; and the Day of Tarwiyah; and the Day of 'Arafah; and when you wash a dead person or shroud him or touch him after he has become cold; and the day of Friday. The ghusl of janabah is obligatory, and the ghusl for the eclipse, when the entire disc is obscured, then perform ghusl.
Then he said, may Allah Most High support him: And the ghusl of the night of al-Fitr is sunnah. And that which indicates it.

key_terms.الْجُمُعَةِ: Friday, a day on which ghusl is prescribed
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: the two sacred sanctuaries whose entry is linked with ghusl
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath prescribed on specific occasions
key_terms.الْكُسُوفِ: the eclipse, for which ghusl is mentioned when the whole disc is obscured
key_terms.غُسْلُ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath made obligatory due to janabah
key_terms.لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ: the night hoped for on the twenty-third night
key_terms.يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ: the Day of 'Arafah, one of the prescribed occasions for ghusl

ai.seo_question: On which occasions is ghusl prescribed in this hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith enumerates occasions in which ghusl is prescribed, including specific nights of Ramadan, major days connected to hajj, Friday, and matters related to the deceased. It also distinguishes between obligatory ghusl, such as ghusl al-janabah, and recommended ghusl, such as the ghusl of the night of al-Fitr.
